facts: Notebook (feed): The Oaks are 8-1 after an 0-9 start through rookie camp and the preseason. Was the 0-9 really about rest and experiments, as Elliot Abraham said in C111, or did the team change something, and will Abraham say so now that it is working? Has the Draymond Green situation settled for him? Is this a defensive team now, or does Wilson Shepard's offense still have another gear? How much of Mike Paulson's attention does the A's offseason take from the Oaks? And with Jerami Grant's failed medical still with the league, what does the roster look like when the hard part of the schedule arrives?
Oaks — season-state (early-season), C116: Was the 0-9 start by design, and is this a defensive team now?

Notebook (feed): Ten games into their first season, the Oakland Oaks are the number one team in the NBA.com power rankings, ranked first of all 31 teams, and holding the top spot from the week before. The rankings are built on season record and recent form, and the Oaks had both: 9-1 when they came out, 3-0 over the last week, 6-1 over the last two weeks. They earned it against real opponents. Four of the teams in the top nine are teams the Oaks have already beaten: Detroit, ranked 3rd, beaten 91-78 on the road; Oklahoma City, ranked 4th, beaten 101-95 in the Cup opener at home; New York, ranked 6th, beaten 115-93 on the road; and Philadelphia, ranked 8th, beaten 120-106 on the road after trailing by two going into the fourth. Ranked 2nd was San Antonio. The rankings only update once a week, and these came out a game behind. Since then the Spurs came into Oakland for a Cup game and won 126-117, handing the Oaks their first ever home loss. So number one is now 9-2, number two is 8-2, and the gap at the top is half a game. For an expansion team that went 0-9 through rookie camp and the preseason, with a first-year head coach and a first-time GM, being ranked first in the league at all is the story.
Oaks — team-update (early-season), C116: Number one in the NBA in year one: the Oaks top the power rankings, a game before the Spurs came to town

sources.name: Wilson Shepard
sources.quote: The team's performance so far has been great, we're 8-1 and the guys are playing with confidence. I think we've found our rhythm, and it's a testament to the hard work they've been putting in. The offense is clicking, and we're getting good contributions from everyone. Of course, we had a hiccup against San Antonio, but that's to be expected. We're still a young team, and we're learning as we go. Overall, I'm proud of how we're performing, and I'm excited to see how we'll do as the season progresses.

sources.name: Melton Neilon
sources.quote: To be honest, Mark Aitken leaving still has me a bit down. I keep thinking about what it means for the A's and the community. It's not just about the player; it's about what he represents. I try not to overthink it, but it's hard not to feel a little empty knowing he's gone.

sources.name: Elliot Abraham
sources.quote: I've seen the fans are excited, and it's infectious. The team's turnaround has really brought them out, and you can feel the energy. We're 8-1 now after a tough start, and it's like a different team. The confidence in the room is palpable, and it's translating to the stands.

sources.name: Mike Paulson
sources.quote: As a resident of West Oakland, I've seen the mood around the Oaks shift dramatically. The team was 0-9 to start, and now they're 8-1. The fans are excited, and you can feel the confidence in the air. It's not just about the wins, though; it's about the team's performance and how they've gelled. I've heard people talking about whether the early struggles were by design, and now they're curious to see if this is a sustainable change. The energy is positive, and it's great to see the community rallying around the team.

approvedQuotes.text: The team's performance so far has been great, we're 8-1 and the guys are playing with confidence. I think we've found our rhythm, and it's a testament to the hard work they've been putting in. The offense is clicking, and we're getting good contributions from everyone. Overall, I'm proud of how we're performing, and I'm excited to see how we'll do as the season progresses.

To be honest, Mark Aitken leaving still has me a bit down. I keep thinking about what it means for the A's and the community. It's not just about the player; it's about what he represents. I try not to overthink it, but it's hard not to feel a little empty knowing he's gone.

I've seen the fans are excited, and it's infectious. The team's turnaround has really brought them out, and you can feel the energy. We're 8-1 now after a tough start, and it's like a different team. The confidence in the room is palpable, and it's translating to the stands.

It's not just about the wins, though; it's about the team's performance and how they've gelled. I've heard people talking about whether the early struggles were by design, and now they're curious to see if this is a sustainable change. The energy is positive, and it's great to see the community rallying around the team.
